stem:
Alok may use only the digits $1$, $4$ and $8$. He wants a $3$-digit palindrome for a locker code.

Which number is a $3$-digit palindrome he can make?

options.text: $148$, claiming it is a palindrome even though the hundreds digit $1$ and the units digit $8$ differ.
$414$, because it reads the same forwards and backwards and uses only allowed digits.
Saying a number is a palindrome is what creates matching hundreds and units digits.
$41$, treated as a $3$-digit palindrome by the same rule.

teacher.key_rationale: 414 reads the same both ways and uses only 1,4,8. 148 omits the matching-ends condition. Saying the palindrome label creates the digit match reverses the relation. Treating 41 as a 3-digit palindrome over-scopes the digit-length rule.
